name: 01-refined-classic
title: Refined Classic
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE high fidelity, production-plausible desktop UI design concept for Kestrel, a keyboard-first Linux/Omarchy file manager. This is a proposed redesign, not a marketing page. Use the supplied existing Kestrel screenshot as a REFERENCE for the product, content, and palette, not an edit target. Make a single full-window horizontal app screenshot, approximately 1600x1000, perfectly front-facing, edge to edge UI, no device mockup, no desktop wallpaper, no comparison collage, no presentation board, no surrounding captions. Minimal, practical native desktop software with readable typography and dense but comfortable rows, crisp aligned columns, consistent 1.5px small line icons. All controls should have believable spacing and function. Avoid card-based dashboard styling, gradients, glow, blur, heavy shadows, giant headings, macOS traffic lights, rounded pills, fake charts, and decorative metrics. A few 4px corner radii only where appropriate. Real rows and files, useful empty space below rows. Preserve discoverable tabs, a breadcrumb path, back/forward/up, view choice, search, and preview access; reduce redundant chrome. Keep a bottom status/progress strip with a small inline progress bar and the exact text 'Copying 12 files', '42 MB/s', 'ETA 8s'. Treat all colors as semantic slots from the active Omarchy theme: canvas #060B1E, darker panel #040816, raised/selected surfaces #131a3a and #252e56, primary text warm peach #ffcead, subdued readable secondary text #a69aa9, muted #6d7db6, accent violet #7d82d9, folder yellow #E9BB4F. These colors MUST stay consistent across all four concepts; use violet sparingly for the active item and progress, no fixed-brand color outside this theme. Strong readable text contrast. Use small warm yellow folder icons, otherwise mostly monochrome line icons. Font appearance: clean native sans UI around 14-15px equivalent at 1440px width, tabular monospace for file sizes and dates. Small section labels not giant or all caps everywhere. The selected image '01-alpine-dawn.png' shows a muted pastel geometric mountain landscape with a peach sun, pale lavender sky, dark navy peaks, matching the reference artwork. Other visible filenames may include '02-coastal-haze.png', '03-desert-light.png', '04-blue-hour.png', 'contact-sheet.pdf', 'export-notes.md', and folders 'Final', 'Drafts'. Keep onscreen text short, correctly spelled, and readable. Do not print color codes, variant numbers, explanatory annotations or design commentary inside the app.
DIRECTION: REFINED CLASSIC. A refined evolution of Kestrel's familiar layout. A compact 176px labeled sidebar with Places and Bookmarks, Home, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Projects; Projects active. A single narrow tab strip above the main area, tabs 'Exports' and 'Research', active tab distinguished only by a short violet underline. Below, one slim unified navigation row with breadcrumb 'Projects / Aurora / Exports', compact search and view controls at its right. Main content is a broad Details file table (Name, Size, Modified) with comfortable 32px rows; selected alpine image indicated by a faint violet row fill, no enclosing thick panel outline. A right inspector about 280px wide has an image preview at the top, a plain filename underneath and a compact 2-column metadata list, with a lot less dead space than the reference. The inspector aligns with the top of the file table, divided by a single subtle vertical hairline. Main file list occupies at least 60% of usable area. Flat functional desktop chrome, consistent quiet hierarchy. Sidebar, list and preview share one continuous canvas; no rounded containers around whole panels. Progress strip spans the bottom with operation title at left and readable speed, ETA, and bar grouped to the right.

File-centric with 32px rows and believable native desktop information density. Flat edges, no floating panels, no nested cards.
